title: Two Buffers, a Self-Spec, Respelling & a Playhead
description: Five drops that swap a recording for a rule: pixel light, live measurement, letter-wise respelling, a pointer field, a scrubbable frame.

drops.title: Two Buffers, One Pixel
drops.description: Four pixel effects, each a pure function of time writing into an opaque colour buffer and an additive light buffer.
drops.concept: pixelfx stores every effect as a tiny code file rather than a sprite sheet: a pure effect exports draw(p, t, o) so the loop tiles without a seam, and randomness is seeded so frame t always renders identically. This rebuild keeps the two-buffer idea — colour for the opaque, dithered pixels and a separate light buffer for additive glow — and lets you watch the light pass on its own.
drops.source: patch-gg/pixelfx — 244 pixel art effects as code

interaction.mouse: Pick an effect from the live thumbnail strip; every thumbnail renders the same clock.
interaction.click: Switch the hero effect, toggle dithering, or show the light buffer by itself.
interaction.touch: Tap a thumbnail to promote it; the panel drops below the stage on narrow screens.

drops.title: The Layout Measures Itself
drops.description: Dimension rules, padding hatching, gap bands, anatomy pins and a baseline grid, all read live off the rendered DOM.
drops.concept: speccer annotates a design system from the component itself rather than from a static mock-up. This version declares what to annotate with data-spec-* attributes, then measures with getBoundingClientRect() and getComputedStyle() into one overlay element — so resizing the window redraws every callout and the spec can never go stale.

interaction.mouse: Toggle each annotation layer independently and cycle the ink palette.
interaction.click: Dimensions, spacing, anatomy pins and typography each switch on and off.
interaction.touch: Everything is re-measured on resize, so the overlay follows the reflowed layout.

drops.title: Words That Respell Themselves
drops.description: Letters paired by position: a shared prefix held sharp, paired glyphs blurring out and swapping back, extras writing on with a glow.
drops.concept: respell is a positional morph, not a diff — index i of the old string is paired with index i of the new one. Leading characters that already match are held sharp, paired letters run swapOut then swapIn, surplus letters backspace and new ones write on with a glow, and the stagger runs backward whenever the word shrinks.
drops.source: PriyanshuMallick/respell — letter-wise text morph for web and Flutter

interaction.mouse: Tune stagger, blur, glow and rate; cycle the wave between auto, forward, backward and together.
interaction.click: Click any line to respell it immediately; the three lines also cycle on their own.
interaction.touch: Tap a line to advance it; the control panel moves below the stack on narrow screens.

drops.title: The Surface Is a Field
drops.description: Four grids — settle, warp, pillars and twist — where every cell reads its distance to the pointer and springs to a target transform.
drops.concept: Textures turn a flat sheet of elements into something that answers to the cursor: each cell computes its own falloff from the pointer and springs toward a transform, so the material deforms locally and recovers on exit. Four of the free textures are rebuilt here on one shared field model with a live radius, force and spring.

interaction.mouse: Move over any panel to push the field around; radius, force, spring and density are all live.
interaction.click: Idle drift can be switched off so the panels rest until you touch them.
interaction.touch: Drag on a panel — pointer capture keeps the field following your finger.

drops.title: Components You Can Scrub
drops.description: A terminal session, a text reveal and a logo assemble, each rendered as a pure function of one frame number you can drag backwards.
drops.concept: snapcn builds product-demo components for Remotion, where every component is a function of the current frame rather than a running animation. Rebuilt in the DOM, that property is the whole demo: one clock drives three components, and scrubbing the playhead — forward, backward, a frame at a time — always lands on exactly the same picture.
drops.source: shadcn-labs/snapcn — Remotion components for product demos

interaction.mouse: Drag the playhead to scrub all three components at once; change fps, duration and stagger live.
interaction.click: Play and pause the shared clock.
interaction.touch: The scrubber and transport sit above the fold; the panel stacks on narrow screens.
interaction.keyboard: Arrow keys step one frame, Space toggles playback.
